change: NTSDAndroid: --original-window (files/args.txt, the app's argument channel) sets NTSDAndroidWindowHost.original; one-to-one = original && not the game's popup, computed per window at present and carried with each frame through the presenter thread (stored with the frame under Target's lock; redraw reuses it); the buffer is then the surface's own size, so the frame is drawn at one device pixel per pixel, centred, without compositor scaling; a surface smaller than the frame is fitted as by default; touches map with the last presentation. Device pixels, not dp: 794x550 dp does not fit a 720 px tall phone. load_memory.py: --game-arg now reaches Android runs (files/args.txt). The iPad needs no code: it shares the S1 view (NTSDGameView) and its original mode.

ipad.scenario: ios_app.py vs on the iPad Air 13-inch (M4) simulator: equal; vs frames identical to the CoreText reference (6/6, 1,826 digests; the other 9 scenarios were not run here)

originalModeCost.reading: the opt-in original mode costs about +1.0 ms process CPU per tick (28.43 vs 27.38: the presenter thread fills a full-surface buffer, ~1.7x the pixels on the A12) and main 11.07 vs 10.89 ms per tick (sets not interleaved); both well under 16.67 ms; the default mode is unaffected

review: Independent, read-only: OK — the flag travels with its frame under the lock, ordering at Alt+Enter holds, touches map with the same centring, a new surface clears the geometry, the default path is unchanged. Low: the Alt+Enter round trip in original mode (checked on both devices: back to 794x550), the opt-in mode's cost (measured), recorded: no in-app switch on Android (S6 documents args.txt), device pixels rather than dp (recorded), iPad taps not exercised.
boundaries: iPad taps not exercised (tvOS has no touch): the original mode's touch mapping (scale 1) is untried on a device
Android: the flag needs adb (files/args.txt); no in-app switch
Android nearest scaling for the default not attempted: the compositor's filtering kept
The original mode's border fill each frame costs ~1 ms CPU on the A12 (clearing borders only after a geometry change would save it; not done)
